mistakes: Offering a private reply on a comment older than 7 days.
Planning an automatic DM reply after the 24-hour window has closed.

b.pass: Ten real messages with names removed, each with intent, the actions its platform allows at that age, the best action and the reply, and no reply that breaks a window rule or shows personal details in public.
b.redo: Send it back if any reply is not allowed on its platform, a public reply has personal details, or the allowed actions are missing.

s.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's inbox for Facebook and Instagram.

  1. Webhook: one n8n Webhook for Page comments, Messenger, Instagram comments and DMs. Answer Meta's verification request once; check every event's signature with the app secret.
  2. Inbox row: platform, kind, item_id, thread_id, author_handle, text, received_at, last_customer_msg_at, status; skip duplicate item_ids.
  3. Classify: the 5.3 labeller adds intent and urgent.
  4. Allowed actions (Code), from the lesson: public unless a DM; private only on a Meta comment within 7 days and not already sent; DM only within 24 hours of the customer's last message; auto only for question, praise or lead and not urgent.
  5. Agent: Sage Desk with get_price, check_delivery_zone, save_lead, handover_to_tolu; structured output { action, public_text, private_text, lead }.
  6. Gate (Code): reject any action not in allowed. auto → send; otherwise Telegram approval.
  7. Send: Graph API reply, private reply (then mark private_sent), DM in thread, hide, or Telegram hand-over with summary and draft.
  8. Watchdog every 10 minutes: questions waiting over 5 minutes, complaints over 60, alert Tolu.

Planted tests (test page and test accounts)

TestExpectedResult
IG comment "how much?" (fresh)Private reply, lead saved1 min 40 s; lead with source link
FB comment from 9 days agoPublic reply onlyPublic; private blocked by code
IG DM, last message 30 h agoTo a personTelegram hand-over
Spam comment with linkHidden, no replyHidden
Angry complaintAcknowledge, hand overTolu answered in 22 min
Same webhook event twiceProcessed onceSecond skipped

Public replies never contained names, addresses, order numbers or phones.
mistakes: Letting the agent decide what is allowed instead of computing it in code.
Posting 'DM sent' publicly before the private reply actually succeeded.
No duplicate check, so retried webhook events get two replies.
s.pass: Executions show a price question answered in under 5 minutes, the expired-window DM handed to a person, the spam comment hidden, and the code gate blocking an action outside the allowed list.
s.redo: Send it back if any test reply breaks a platform rule, the expired-window DM was answered by the bot, spam got a reply, or there is no hand-over path.

g.answer:
Worked example: Bloom Bakes, a fictional cake shop in Abeokuta, two weeks on Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, with X mentions polled every 15 minutes on a small budget.

MeasureTwo weeks beforeTwo weeks with the agent
Messages and comments312341
Median first response, questions2 h 40 min1 min 50 s
Median first response, complaints6 h41 min (person)
Unanswered after 24 h583
Spam hiddennot tracked27

Leads captured with source and consent: Instagram 31 · Facebook 12 · WhatsApp 9 · X 1. Of these, 22 agreed to a follow-up and 14 ordered.

Hand-overs: 19 (11 complaints, 5 big orders such as wedding cakes, 3 asked for a person). Two waited past the 60-minute target on a Sunday; the watchdog fired both times.

Complaints about the bot: none. One customer asked "Is this a robot?" and the reply said it was the shop's assistant and offered the owner.

Rule checks: 0 replies outside the 24-hour window, 0 second private replies, 0 personal details in public replies (checked by a code scan of all public texts).

Submit: this table, the before figures and where they came from (page inbox export), the leads table with sources, the hand-over log and the owner's comment.
mistakes: No measured 'before' response time to compare against.
Counting the same customer as several leads across platforms.
Saving leads with no source link or consent flag.
Letting the bot argue with angry customers instead of handing over.
g.pass: Two weeks of data with median response time against the previous two weeks, leads by platform with source and consent, a hand-over count, and no complaints about the bot.
g.redo: Send it back if response time did not improve, there is no baseline, leads lack source or consent, or customers complained about the bot.
